title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing §8.5). X is smooth projective of dimension n over a perfect field k of characteristic p, embedded in P^r. Y is a smooth hypersurface section of degree d, of dimension n-1. H^i denotes crystalline cohomology over W = W(k). The subscript ss denotes the Frobenius-semisimple (stable, bijective) part of a finite k-space with a p-linear endomorphism, in the Hasse–Witt / Fitting-decomposition sense.

The previous page sets up the following objects.
- E(Y) = Coker(H^{n-1}(X) -> H^{n-1}(Y)) is the crystalline vanishing cohomology, which is torsion-free.
- E(Y,O_Y) = Coker v is the coherent vanishing cohomology, where v: H^{n-1}(X,O_X)_ss -> H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y)_ss.
- These fit in the exact sequence (8.5.1): 0 -> Ker v -> (_pTors^n(X))_ss -> (E(Y)⊗k)_ss -φ-> E(Y,O_Y)_ss -> 0.
- Over a finite field, dim (E(Y)⊗k)_ss is the number of eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on vanishing cohomology that are p-adic units. This is the multiplicity of slope 0, i.e. the unit-root part.

This page.
- (8.5.6): surjectivity of φ alone gives dim(E(Y)⊗k)_ss >= dim E(Y,O_Y)_ss. So the number of unit-root Frobenius eigenvalues on vanishing cohomology is bounded below by the stable rank of the coherent vanishing cohomology. A deleted variant subtracted a 'number of p-torsion coefficients' t^{n-1}(X,p) of crystalline cohomology.
- Remark 8.5.7: Grothendieck believes v is always injective. He notes it holds when H^{n-1}(X,O_X(-d)) = 0, from 0 -> O_X(-d) -> O_X -> O_Y -> 0. By Serre duality this group is H^1(X,ω_X(d))^∨, which vanishes for d large. A deleted remark about combining dim Coker w - dim Ker w (the old cup-product map w by the polarization) belongs to an abandoned version.
- 8.5.8: take Y a general degree-d section, so that the ss-rank of E(Y,O_Y) is maximal (generic). By (8.5.5), the right side, hence the number of unit-root eigenvalues, is then independent of Y, up to the term dim Ker v (presumably 0, and 0 for d large).
- Consequence for k finite: there is a dense open U_d in the projective space of degree-d hypersurfaces such that, for every point of U_d rational over a finite extension k', the number of p-adic-unit Frobenius eigenvalues on the vanishing cohomology of Y_{k'bar} is constant.

Aim (continued on the next page). Show that this number is nonzero for d large, i.e. the vanishing motive E(Y) of the generic section has maximal 'niveau' n-1. Via (8.5.6) it suffices that the generic dim E(Y,O_Y)_ss > 0 for d large, which is said to be proved in n°7. The next page reinterprets everything as an exact sequence of étale F_p-local systems / π_1(U_d)-representations over U_d.

This is a study of the unit-root (ordinary) part of the vanishing cohomology of hypersurface sections, linked to p-torsion in crystalline H^n(X). It is a precursor to generic-ordinarity questions.
errors: Not an error but an open guess that can be closed: v is injective on semisimple parts in general (for n >= 2). Let x ∈ Ker v ∩ H^{n-1}(X,O_X)_ss. Then x is the image of some y ∈ H^{n-1}(X,O_X(-Y)). F^m x is the image of F^m y ∈ H^{n-1}(X,O_X(-p^m Y)), and that group vanishes for m large by Serre duality and Serre vanishing. So F^m x = 0, and bijectivity of F on the ss part gives x = 0. Grothendieck only states injectivity as a belief, under the hypothesis H^{n-1}(X,O_X(-d)) = 0.
Residual inconsistency of the revision: struck passages still refer to w and Coker w, which were removed from (8.5.1) on the previous page. The surviving text is consistent.

The constancy claim in 8.5.8 is stated 'up to the term -dim Ker v'. Since dim Ker v is also upper semicontinuous, the argument implicitly needs either Ker v = 0 or a further genericity condition. This is harmless given the argument above.

ideas.what: Unit-root eigenvalues of Frobenius on vanishing crystalline cohomology bounded below by the stable (Hasse–Witt semisimple) rank of coherent vanishing cohomology H^{n-1}(Y,O)/H^{n-1}(X,O); defect controlled by p-torsion in crystalline H^n(X).
ideas.modern_name: slope-0 part of crystalline cohomology vs. Hasse–Witt / stable rank of H^i(O) (Bloch–Illusie–Katz: H^i(X,W O)⊗K slope [0,1) part; unit-root F-crystal)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz, Bloch, Illusie (de Rham–Witt, 1970s); Artin–Mazur for formal groups

ideas.what: Number of p-adic-unit Frobenius eigenvalues is constant on a dense open subset of the parameter space of hypersurface sections.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck specialization theorem for Newton polygons (slope-0 multiplicity), generic Newton polygon
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Barsotti 1970; Montréal 1970/74), proof in Katz 'Slope filtration of F-crystals' (1979)
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1974), in the context of the specialization theorem

ideas.what: Injectivity of H^{n-1}(X,O_X)_ss -> H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y)_ss for an ample smooth section Y.
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius-stable Kodaira-type vanishing / injectivity (F-stable part of H^i(X,O(-D)) vanishes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Hartshorne–Speiser / Lyubeznik-style Frobenius arguments, Mehta–Ramanathan context

ideas.what: Nonvanishing of the unit-root part of vanishing cohomology for generic high-degree sections is equivalent to (or implies) the vanishing motive having maximal niveau n-1.
ideas.modern_name: generic ordinarity / Hodge level vs. Newton polygon (Mazur–Ogus 'Newton above Hodge'); Illusie's generic ordinarity of complete intersections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mazur, Ogus (1972–73); Deligne–Illusie, Illusie 'Ordinarité des intersections complètes générales' (1990)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, for an arbitrary smooth projective X in char p, the problem of showing that the vanishing cohomology of a general hypersurface section of high degree has a nonzero unit-root part (maximal niveau). He links this to p-torsion in crystalline H^n(X). Illusie proved full generic ordinarity for complete intersections in projective space; for hypersurface sections of an arbitrary X, the torsion-sensitive exact sequence (8.5.1) relating unit-root rank, coherent vanishing cohomology and _pTors^n(X) is not something I recognise from the literature.
missed.quote: le nombre de valeurs propres de Frobenius opérant sur la cohomologie évanescente de Y_{k'} et qui sont des unités p-adiques soit constant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives an explicit mechanism by which crystalline p-torsion of X obstructs ordinarity of hypersurface sections. This is relevant to generic ordinarity questions for sections of non-ordinary or torsion-bearing varieties.

missed.claim: Conjectured injectivity of v on semisimple parts. It is provable in a few lines by a Frobenius iteration plus Serre vanishing, which would remove the 'Ker v' error term throughout 8.5.
missed.quote: Je pense que l'homomorphisme v de (8.5.2) est injectif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: it closes the stated gap and makes (8.5.5) an equality of unit-root rank = coherent stable rank + dim _pTors^n(X)_ss.

deep.surprise_reason: These are early (late-1960s) crystalline notes in which Grothendieck anticipates the specialization theorem for slope-0 multiplicities and generic ordinarity of hypersurface sections. He also ties the unit-root rank to p-torsion in crystalline cohomology via an explicit exact sequence. The individual statements are mostly now known (Katz, Illusie), but this formulation is unpublished.
